newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC moves to streamline customs, tariffs.
newsitem.headline: APEC moves to streamline customs, tariffs.

text.p: APEC members plan to revise customs and tariff procedures to ease and streamline trade around the Pacific Rim, leaders of the 18 Asia-Pacific economies said in a statement following their annual summit on Monday.
Confusing terminology, lack of transparency, non-tariff barriers and corruption are among impediments to trade in many parts of the world.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum aims at achieving a tariff-free zone for trade and investment by the year 2020.
"This year we have made our tariff regimes more transparent," the APEC leaders said in their statement.

"We have agreed to harmonise our tariff nomenclature by the end of this year and our customs clearance procedures by 1998. We have agreed to align our national standards with international standards and to recognise each other's national standards," the statement said.
The APEC leaders told their ministers to intensify efforts to simplify customs clearance procedures.

They should also work on implementing commitments on protecting intellectual property rights, harmonising customs valuation, facilitating a comprehensive trade in services and enhancing the environment for investments.

"We reaffirm the primacy of an open, multilateral trading system based on the WTO" -- the World Trade Organisation regulating international trade that holds its first ministerial conference in Singapore next month.

APEC includes Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and United States.
